title: Section 73 ICA — Compensation for loss caused by breach

content.overview: The party suffering from breach is entitled to compensation for loss which naturally arose in the usual course of things, or which the parties knew when they made the contract to be likely to result from the breach. Remote loss is excluded; mitigation is required.

sections.heading: Two limbs
sections.body: Limb 1: ordinary natural consequences. Limb 2: special loss within contemplation of both parties at formation. Explanation: means existing to remedy the inconvenience must be considered (mitigation).

sections.heading: Track B
sections.body: Plead general and special damages separately with quantum evidence. Special damages need proof of knowledge at formation. Check arbitration clauses for forum.

illustrations: A contracts to deliver goods to B by a specified date and fails, causing ordinary market loss naturally flowing from the delay; section 73 provides the starting measure for compensation.

enhancement.detailedExplanation:
India Code rule: Section 73 entitles a party suffering breach to compensation for loss that naturally arose in the usual course from the breach or was within the parties’ contemplation when contracting, but excludes remote and indirect loss.

Definition: Section 73 is the principal statutory measure of damages for breach of contract.

Ingredients:
1. Establish a contract and breach.
2. Identify actual loss caused by the breach.
3. Show that the loss naturally arose or was within contemplation when contracting.
4. Exclude remote or indirect loss.
5. Consider reasonable mitigation of loss.
